docs.title: Reports API Documentation
docs.text:
A practical REST API documentation project built with Markdown, Postman, MkDocs Material, and GitHub Pages.

This project demonstrates how technical writers can structure API documentation to help developers understand endpoints, configure requests, and interpret API responses.

View API Reference · About This Project

docs.title: Project Overview
docs.text:
The Reports API provides access to generated reports through a RESTful API.

This documentation covers the request configuration, query parameters, response structure, and report object fields for the reports endpoint.

docs.title: API Information
docs.text: Item Details API Type REST API Base URL https://api.qaautomationlabs.com API Version v1 Response Format JSON Documented Method GET

docs.title: Available Endpoint
docs.text: Method Endpoint Description GET /v1/reports Retrieves a list of reports

docs.title: Request
docs.text:
curl -X GET "https://api.qaautomationlabs.com/v1/reports?page=1&limit=10" \
  -H "Accept: application/json"

docs.title: Request Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Description page integer Specifies the page number to retrieve. limit integer Specifies the maximum number of records requested.

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
The endpoint returned a 200 OK response during Postman testing.

The response contains a data array with report objects.

{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "name": "Sales Report 1",
      "type": "sales",
      "format": "pdf",
      "status": "ready",
      "rows": 20423,
      "generatedAt": "2026-02-21T23:31:53+00:00"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Reports API Documentation project is a technical documentation portfolio project created to demonstrate REST API documentation skills.

The project documents a Reports API endpoint that retrieves a list of generated reports in JSON format.

docs.title: Project Objectives
docs.text:
• Document a REST API endpoint.
  • Explain request parameters and headers.
  • Describe the response structure and data fields.
  • Provide cURL and Postman request examples.
  • Document verified API behavior clearly.
  • Publish documentation as a searchable website.

docs.text: Tool Purpose Markdown Create technical documentation Postman Test API requests and responses GitHub Version control and documentation hosting MkDocs Build the documentation website Material for MkDocs Provide the website theme GitHub Pages Publish the documentation website

docs.title: Documentation Approach
docs.text:
The documentation was created using a user-focused approach.

The content explains how to configure the API request, understand the available parameters, and interpret the response.

Only API behavior verified during testing is documented as confirmed behavior. Unverified error responses are presented as test scenarios rather than established API behavior.

docs.title: Error Reference
docs.text:
This page describes potential HTTP errors that may occur when working with the Reports API.

Documentation status: The successful 200 OK response has been verified through Postman. The error scenarios listed below are provided for documentation planning and require additional API testing for confirmation.

docs.title: HTTP Status Codes
docs.text: Status Code Name Description Verification Status 400 Bad Request The server cannot process the request because of invalid input. Not verified 401 Unauthorized The request requires valid authentication credentials. Not verified 403 Forbidden The server refuses to authorize the request. Not verified 404 Not Found The requested resource could not be found. Not verified 500 Internal Server Error The server encountered an unexpected condition. Not verified

docs.title: Error Testing Scenarios
docs.text: The following scenarios can be used to plan additional API testing.

docs.title: 400 — Bad Request
docs.text:
Scenario: Send an invalid query parameter or unsupported parameter value.

Expected outcome: The API may return a 400 Bad Request response if the request is invalid.

Verification: Not yet performed.

docs.title: 401 — Unauthorized
docs.text:
Scenario: Send the request without required authentication credentials, if authentication is supported.

Expected outcome: The API may return a 401 Unauthorized response.

Verification: Not yet performed.

docs.title: 403 — Forbidden
docs.text:
Scenario: Send a request using credentials that do not have the required permissions, if authorization is supported.

Expected outcome: The API may return a 403 Forbidden response.

Verification: Not yet performed.

docs.title: 404 — Not Found
docs.text:
Scenario: Request a resource or endpoint that does not exist.

Expected outcome: The API may return a 404 Not Found response.

Verification: Not yet performed.

docs.title: 500 — Internal Server Error
docs.text:
Scenario: An unexpected server-side error occurs while processing the request.

Expected outcome: The API may return a 500 Internal Server Error response.

Verification: Not yet performed.

docs.title: Error Handling Guidelines
docs.text:
When troubleshooting an API request:

  1. Verify the request URL and HTTP method.
  2. Check the query parameters and their values.
  3. Confirm that the required headers are included.
  4. Review the HTTP status code returned by the server.
  5. Check the response body for additional error information.
  6. Retry the request only after reviewing the cause of the error.

docs.title: List Reports
docs.text: Retrieves a list of generated reports from the Reports API.

docs.title: Endpoint
docs.text: Item Details Method GET Endpoint /v1/reports Response format JSON

docs.title: Request URL
docs.text: https://api.qaautomationlabs.com/v1/reports?page=1&limit=10

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required Description page integer Not verified Specifies the page number to retrieve. limit integer Not verified Specifies the maximum number of records requested.

Note: Whether these parameters are mandatory or optional has not been verified.

docs.title: Request Headers
docs.text: Header Value Description Accept application/json Indicates that the client expects a JSON response.

docs.title: cURL Example
docs.text:
curl -X GET "https://api.qaautomationlabs.com/v1/reports?page=1&limit=10" \
  -H "Accept: application/json"

docs.title: Postman Configuration
docs.text:
Use the following configuration to test the endpoint in Postman.

Setting Value Method GET URL https://api.qaautomationlabs.com/v1/reports?page=1&limit=10 Header Accept: application/json

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Open Postman.
  2. Create a new HTTP request.
  3. Select the GET method.
  4. Enter the request URL.
  5. Add the Accept: application/json header.
  6. Click Send.
  7. Review the HTTP status code and response body.

docs.title: Response Overview
docs.text:
The response contains a data array. Each element represents a report object.

For information about the response fields, see the Response Reference.

docs.title: HTTP Status Code
docs.text: Status Code Description 200 OK The request was successfully processed, and report data was returned.

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text:
The endpoint accepts page and limit query parameters.

Example:

/v1/reports?page=1&limit=10

The meaning of the parameters is documented based on their use in the tested request. Additional pagination behavior has not been verified.

docs.title: Response Reference
docs.text: This page describes the JSON response structure and fields returned by the Reports API.

docs.title: Response Structure
docs.text:
A successful request returns a JSON object containing a data array.

Each element in the data array represents a report object.

{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "name": "Sales Report 1",
      "type": "sales",
      "format": "pdf",
      "status": "ready",
      "rows": 20423,
      "generatedAt": "2026-02-21T23:31:53+00:00"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Response Overview
docs.text: Property Type Description data array Contains the report objects returned by the API.

docs.title: Report Object
docs.text:
The report object contains information about an individual report.

Field Type Description Example id integer Identifies the report. 1 name string Specifies the name of the report. "Sales Report 1" type string Specifies the report type. "sales" format string Specifies the report format. "pdf" status string Specifies the current report status. "ready" rows integer Specifies the number of rows associated with the report. 20423 generatedAt string Specifies the date and time associated with report generation. "2026-02-21T23:31:53+00:00"

docs.text:
Identifies the report.

Type: integer

Example:

  "id": 1
}

docs.title: type
docs.text:
Specifies the report type.

Example:

docs.title: format
docs.text:
Specifies the report format.

Type: string

Example:

docs.title: status
docs.text:
Specifies the current report status.

Type: string

Example:

{
  "status": "ready"
}

docs.title: rows
docs.text:
Specifies the number of rows associated with the report.

Type: integer

Example:

{
  "rows": 20423
}

docs.title: generatedAt
docs.text:
Specifies the date and time associated with report generation.

Type: string

Example:

{
  "generatedAt": "2026-02-21T23:31:53+00:00"
}

The date-time format and timezone behavior have not been independently verified beyond the returned example.

Postman was used to send the API request, inspect the HTTP response, and review the returned JSON data.

docs.text:
The following observations were recorded during the test:

  • The API returned an HTTP 200 OK status.
  • The response was returned in JSON format.
  • The response contained a data array.
  • Each report object contained report-related fields.
  • The response structure was used to prepare the API response reference documentation.

docs.title: Documentation Workflow
docs.text:
The API testing results supported the following documentation activities:

  1. Identifying the API endpoint and HTTP method.
  2. Documenting the request header.
  3. Reviewing the JSON response structure.
  4. Identifying response fields and their data types.
  5. Creating request and response examples.
  6. Documenting potential error-testing scenarios.

docs.title: Testing Limitations
docs.text:
The following items require additional testing before they can be documented as verified behavior:

  • Authentication requirements.
  • Invalid query parameter handling.
  • Authentication and authorization errors.
  • Resource-not-found behavior.
  • Server-side error responses.
  • Pagination behavior beyond the tested request.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Postman testing helped validate the successful API response and provided the information required to create the API reference and response documentation.

Additional test cases should be performed before documenting unverified API behavior as confirmed functionality.
